scope_note: Native export encoder and decoder selectors, strict native quality/preset metadata, isolated explicit checks and per-instance qualification. Windows uses the existing browser, one temporary tab, against a bounded CPU-only API: legacy defaults, disabled hardware, explicit x264 check, refresh/reopen and saved actual/requested labels. Separate bounded R9700 API checks passed native Vulkan encode/color and actual Vulkan decode/color; three-frame exports verified legacy x264/software and selected Vulkan/Vulkan, without CPU fallback. Both uncached preview frames handed their resident contexts to export. A held shared reservation refused a forced recheck without changing availability. No GPU handles remained at idle; own units stopped and main five unsaved edits/history were preserved. No browser installation, local build/render, foreign workload or driver changes. NVENC/VideoToolbox hardware, long-source format coverage, desktop physical UI, sustained concurrent use and release qualification remain outside this finite check. The existing Windows browser also selected unchecked Vulkan encoder and decoder against the isolated R9700 host, saw Start disabled until each explicit check, received native QP23/no-preset defaults and exported three frames. READY reported actual Vulkan encode/decode without fallback; HTTP output decoded to exactly three 640x360 H.264 frames, 0.125s, no audio. Both test tabs were used sequentially. The R9700 GUI service was capped at one CPU/2GiB/zero swap and left no GPU handles at idle.
